topics: ⚔️ A Catalogue of National Punishments — perverted justice, false oaths, bloodshed, idolatry, and exile, each with its verse
🗣️ Vulgar Speech and Its Price — troubles, harsh decrees, and even a sealed good decree reversed
🩹 Signs of Sin on the Body — hidrokan, jaundice, poverty, and askara as diagnostic markers
🍯 Three Rabbis, Three Fates — Rabbi Yehuda's praise of Rome, Rabbi Yosei's silence, and Rabbi Shimon's rebuke
🕳️ Twelve Years in a Cave — Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai and his son hide from Rome, sustained by a miraculous carob and spring
🌿 Two Myrtle Branches — the old man's answer that reconciles Rabbi Shimon to the world outside the cave

overview.title: 📖 Overview: National Sins and the Cave of Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai
overview.subtitle: Shabbat 33a–33b
overview.hebrewSource: כׇּל הֵיכָא דַּהֲוָה מָחֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, הֲוָה מַסֵּי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf continues its catalogue of sin-and-punishment pairings — perverted justice, false oaths and desecrating Shabbat, bloodshed, forbidden relations and idolatry, neglecting the Sabbatical year, and vulgar speech — each traced to a specific verse of rebuke, and each showing that societal sins bring national catastrophe: sword, wild beasts, exile, destruction of the Temple. The Gemara then catalogues bodily signs of sin (hidrokan, jaundice, poverty, askara) before turning to its most famous narrative: Rabbi Yehuda praised Rome's public works, Rabbi Yosei stayed silent, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai denounced them as self-serving — a comment that reached the authorities and cost Rabbi Shimon a death sentence. He and his son Rabbi Elazar fled to a cave, sustained for twelve years by a miraculous carob tree and spring while immersed in Torah study. Emerging too harshly critical of ordinary working people, they were sent back for another year, and finally reconciled to the world through an old man's simple devotion to Shabbat with two myrtle branches.

slides.title: ⚔️ A Catalogue of National Sins and Punishments
slides.subtitle: Each sin traced to its own verse
rows: Perverted or delayed justice, dereliction in Torah
Sword, looting, famine — bread eaten by weight and never satisfying
Vain and false oaths, desecrating God's name and Shabbat
Wild beasts multiply, domestic animals perish, roads grow desolate
The Temple is destroyed and the Divine Presence departs
Forbidden relations, idolatry, neglecting Sabbatical/Jubilee years
Exile — the land 'expels' its inhabitants as it expelled the nations before them
Troubles multiply, harsh decrees renew, prayers of orphans and widows go unanswered

slides.title: 🩹 Reading the Body for Signs of Sin
slides.subtitle: The Sages diagnose spiritual causes for physical ailments

lines.speaker: Baraita
lines.text: Four signs: hidrokan (edema) for sin, jaundice for baseless hatred, poverty for arrogance, and askara (throat disease) for slander.

lines.speaker: Objection
lines.text: But women, gentiles, and children also get askara — none are obligated in Torah study, so how can dereliction in Torah be its cause?

lines.speaker: Reply
lines.text: Each still causes idleness from Torah: wives distract husbands, gentiles distract Israel, children distract their fathers.

lines.speaker: Final challenge
lines.text: But schoolchildren, who do study, also get askara!

lines.speaker: R' Guryon
lines.text: When there are no righteous adults in the generation, schoolchildren are 'seized' for the generation's sins instead — proven from Song of Songs 1:8's image of lambs held as collateral for negligent shepherds.

slides.title: 🗣️ Three Opinions on Rome — and Three Fates
slides.subtitle: A conversation with fatal consequences

nodes.content: 💬 R' Yehuda: 'How pleasant are Rome's works — they built markets, bridges, bathhouses!'
🔥 R' Shimon bar Yoḥai: 'Everything they built serves only themselves — markets for prostitutes, baths for pampering, bridges to collect tolls!'
⚖️ Yehuda ben Gerim reported this to Rome: Yehuda was elevated, Yosei exiled to Tzippori, and Shimon sentenced to death

slides.title: 🕳️ Twelve Years in the Cave
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai and his son Rabbi Elazar in hiding

steps.content: 1️⃣ They hide first in the study hall, fed daily by Rabbi Shimon's wife, then flee to a cave when the danger grows — fearing she might be tortured into revealing them
2️⃣ A miracle provides a carob tree and spring; they bury themselves in sand to spare their clothing and study Torah all day, dressing only to pray

3️⃣ After twelve years, Elijah announces the emperor's death and the decree's end — but emerging, they see ordinary people plowing and burn what they look upon in disdain for 'abandoning eternal life'
4️⃣ A Divine Voice sends them back for twelve more months: 'Did you come out to destroy My world? Return to your cave!'
5️⃣ Emerging again, an old man running with two myrtle branches for Shabbat — one for 'Remember,' one for 'Observe' — restores their peace of mind about ordinary people's devotion

slides.title: 🌳 Gratitude After the Miracle
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Shimon repairs what troubled the town, following Jacob's example
slides.hebrewSource: וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם... וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר
slides.label: The model:
slides.text: After the cave, Rabbi Shimon's son-in-law Rabbi Pineḥas ben Ya'ir found him physically marked by years of hardship, yet Rabbi Shimon insisted the ordeal had sharpened his Torah — where once Rabbi Pineḥas answered his questions with twelve resolutions, now Rabbi Shimon answered his with twenty-four. Reasoning from Jacob, who came 'whole' to Shechem and then 'graced the city' with civic improvements, Rabbi Shimon resolved that since a miracle had been done for him, he too should repair something for the community's benefit — asking whether there was a problem needing his attention.

summary.principle: National catastrophes trace to specific societal sins in the Torah's own words, the body itself bears diagnostic signs of hidden sin, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai's twelve years in a cave — from denouncing Rome to burning fields in contempt of ordinary labor to being humbled by an old man's simple mitzva devotion — teaches that miraculous salvation calls for gratitude expressed in service to others.

🩹 The body itself signals hidden sin: hidrokan, jaundice, poverty, askara

🕳️ Twelve years in a cave transform R' Shimon's relationship to ordinary people

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: One who experiences a miracle should respond with gratitude expressed through service to others, following Jacob's example at Shechem

quiz.q: According to the Gemara's catalogue, what national catastrophe results from the sin of bloodshed?
o: Famine and drought
The Holy Temple is destroyed and the Divine Presence departs from Israel
Wild beasts multiply
Exile alone, without other consequences
quiz.e: The Gemara derives from Numbers 35:33–34 that bloodshed defiles the land to the point that God's presence can no longer dwell there, leading to the Temple's destruction.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara resolve the objection that women, gentiles, and children — none obligated in Torah study — also suffer from askara if it is caused by dereliction in Torah study?
o: It admits Torah study is not the cause
It explains that each group causes idleness from Torah in others (wives distract husbands, gentiles distract Israel, children distract fathers)
It says askara has multiple unrelated causes
It claims the objection is baseless
quiz.e: The Gemara answers that although these groups are not themselves obligated in Torah study, they can cause others (husbands, Israel, fathers) to become idle from it, and are punished accordingly.

quiz.q: What happened to Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosei, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai after their conversation about Rome's public works was reported to the authorities?
o: All three were exiled equally
Rabbi Yehuda was elevated for praising Rome, Rabbi Yosei was exiled to Tzippori for his silence, and Rabbi Shimon was sentenced to death for his criticism
All three were executed
Nothing happened to any of them
quiz.e: Yehuda ben Gerim reported the conversation to the Roman authorities, resulting in different fates matched to each sage's stance: praise, silence, and denunciation.

quiz.q: What sustained Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai and his son Rabbi Elazar during their twelve years hiding in a cave?
o: Food smuggled in by students
A miraculous carob tree and spring of water
They fasted the entire time
Supplies from Rabbi Shimon's wife
quiz.e: The Gemara relates that a miracle provided a carob tree and a spring of water, which sustained them throughout their twelve years in hiding.

quiz.q: What finally reconciled Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai to the world of ordinary people after he emerged from the cave a second time?
o: A letter from the Roman emperor
Seeing an elderly man running with two myrtle branches in honor of Shabbat, one for 'Remember' and one for 'Observe'
A vision from Elijah the Prophet
A ruling from the Sanhedrin
quiz.e: Witnessing the old man's simple, joyful devotion to the mitzva of honoring Shabbat with two myrtle branches showed Rabbi Shimon how beloved the mitzvot were to ordinary Israel, putting his mind at ease.
